cards.front: What are the key features of osteoarthritis?
cards.back: **Mechanical wear** of articular cartilage, not systemic inflammation. Joint space narrowing, **subchondral sclerosis**, cysts and **osteophytes**. In the hand: **DIP** (**Heberden nodes**) and **PIP** (**Bouchard nodes**). Pain worsens with use; morning stiffness is brief.
cards.back_pt: **Desgaste mecânico** da cartilagem articular, sem inflamação sistêmica. Redução do espaço articular, **esclerose subcondral**, cistos e **osteófitos**. Na mão: **IFD** (**nódulos de Heberden**) e **IFP** (**nódulos de Bouchard**). A dor piora com o uso; a rigidez matinal é curta.

cards.front: What drives joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis, and which markers support the diagnosis?
cards.back: Autoimmune synovitis linked to **HLA-DR4** (smoking is a risk factor). Inflamed synovium forms **pannus** that erodes cartilage and bone. **Anti-CCP** (anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide) is the most specific antibody; **rheumatoid factor** (IgM against the Fc of IgG) is less specific.
cards.back_pt: Sinovite autoimune associada ao **HLA-DR4** (o tabagismo é fator de risco). A sinóvia inflamada forma o **pannus**, que erode cartilagem e osso. O **anti-CCP** (antipeptídeo citrulinado cíclico) é o anticorpo mais específico; o **fator reumatoide** (IgM contra o Fc da IgG) é menos específico.

cards.front: Name classic features of rheumatoid arthritis beyond the small joints of the hands.
cards.back: **Rheumatoid nodules** (central fibrinoid necrosis with palisading histiocytes), **interstitial lung disease**, **anemia of chronic disease**, **Felty syndrome** (RA + splenomegaly + neutropenia), **Baker cyst** behind the knee, and **atlantoaxial subluxation**.
cards.back_pt: **Nódulos reumatoides** (necrose fibrinoide central com histiócitos em paliçada), **doença pulmonar intersticial**, **anemia de doença crônica**, **síndrome de Felty** (AR + esplenomegalia + neutropenia), **cisto de Baker** atrás do joelho e **subluxação atlantoaxial**.

cards.front: What are the classic findings of ankylosing spondylitis?
cards.back: Usually a young man, **HLA-B27**, RF negative. Inflammatory low back pain that **improves with exercise**; **sacroiliitis** and **enthesitis**. Spinal fusion gives a **bamboo spine** and less chest expansion. Also **anterior uveitis** and **aortic regurgitation** (aortitis).
cards.back_pt: Geralmente homem jovem, **HLA-B27**, FR negativo. Lombalgia inflamatória que **melhora com o exercício**; **sacroileíte** e **entesite**. A fusão da coluna causa a **coluna em bambu** (*bamboo spine*) e menor expansibilidade torácica. Também **uveíte anterior** e **insuficiência aórtica** (aortite).

cards.front: Which joint findings suggest psoriatic arthritis?
cards.back: **DIP joint** involvement with **nail pitting**, **dactylitis** (*sausage digits*), and a **pencil-in-cup** deformity on x-ray. It is a seronegative spondyloarthropathy (HLA-B27 related, mainly when the spine is involved) and can occur with mild or no skin disease.
cards.back_pt: Acometimento das **articulações IFD** com **pitting ungueal** (depressões puntiformes nas unhas), **dactilite** (*sausage digits*, dedos em salsicha) e deformidade em **lápis na taça** (*pencil-in-cup*) na radiografia. É uma espondiloartropatia soronegativa (associada ao HLA-B27, principalmente quando há acometimento da coluna) e pode ocorrer com pouca ou nenhuma lesão de pele.

cards.front: How do gout and pseudogout crystals look under polarized light?
cards.back: **Gout** (monosodium urate): **needle-shaped**, **negatively birefringent**, yellow when parallel to the compensator axis. **Pseudogout** (calcium pyrophosphate): **rhomboid**, **weakly positively birefringent**, blue when parallel.
cards.back_pt: **Gota** (urato monossódico): cristais **em agulha**, com **birrefringência negativa**, amarelos quando paralelos ao eixo do compensador. **Pseudogota** (pirofosfato de cálcio): cristais **romboides**, com **birrefringência fracamente positiva**, azuis quando paralelos.

cards.front: What are the two mechanisms of hyperuricemia in gout?
cards.back: **Underexcretion** (most cases): CKD, **thiazide** and **loop diuretics**, alcohol, low-dose aspirin. **Overproduction**: high cell turnover (**tumor lysis**, myeloproliferative disease) and **HGPRT deficiency** (Lesch-Nyhan; see biochemistry). Gout often begins as **podagra**; chronic deposits form **tophi**.
cards.back_pt: **Hipoexcreção** (maioria dos casos): DRC, **diuréticos tiazídicos** e **de alça**, álcool, ácido acetilsalicílico em dose baixa. **Hiperprodução**: alta renovação celular (**lise tumoral**, doença mieloproliferativa) e **deficiência de HGPRT** (Lesch-Nyhan; ver bioquímica). A gota costuma começar como **podagra**; depósitos crônicos formam **tofos**.

cards.front: What are the typical features and associations of pseudogout (CPPD disease)?
cards.back: Older adult, acute arthritis usually of the **knee** or wrist. X-ray shows **chondrocalcinosis** (calcified cartilage). Associations: **hemochromatosis**, **hyperparathyroidism**, **hypomagnesemia** and **hypophosphatasia**.
cards.back_pt: Idoso com artrite aguda, geralmente do **joelho** ou punho. A radiografia mostra **condrocalcinose** (calcificação da cartilagem). Associações: **hemocromatose**, **hiperparatireoidismo**, **hipomagnesemia** e **hipofosfatasia**.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman has 5 days of fever and pain that moved from her wrists to her ankles. She is sexually active with a new partner. Temperature is 38.4°C. There is pain and swelling along the tendons on the back of her right hand, and a few small painless pustules on a red base on her forearms and lower legs. She has no eye symptoms or dysuria. Her left knee is red, warm and swollen. Synovial fluid is cloudy with 56,000 WBC/µL (90% neutrophils) and no crystals. The Gram stain shows no organisms. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Migratory polyarthralgia, **tenosynovitis** and painless **pustules** in a young sexually active adult point to **disseminated gonococcal infection**. The synovial fluid is in the septic range (above about 50,000 WBC/µL, mostly neutrophils), and a Gram stain with no organisms is common with *N. gonorrhoeae*. *S. aureus* is the most common cause of septic arthritis overall, but it usually affects one joint without tenosynovitis or skin pustules. *C. trachomatis* causes reactive arthritis, which starts weeks after the infection, often with conjunctivitis and urethritis, and the joint is sterile.
questions.explanation_pt: Poliartralgia migratória, **tenossinovite** e **pústulas** indolores em adulto jovem sexualmente ativo indicam **infecção gonocócica disseminada**. O líquido sinovial está na faixa séptica (acima de cerca de 50.000 leucócitos/µL, com predomínio de neutrófilos), e a ausência de bactérias na coloração de Gram é comum com *N. gonorrhoeae*. O *S. aureus* é a causa mais comum de artrite séptica em geral, mas costuma acometer uma única articulação, sem tenossinovite nem pústulas. A *C. trachomatis* causa artrite reativa, que surge semanas após a infecção, muitas vezes com conjuntivite e uretrite, e a articulação é estéril.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man wakes at night with severe pain in his right big toe. He drank a lot of beer at a party the evening before. Six weeks ago he started hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension. The first metatarsophalangeal joint is red, hot, swollen and very tender. Temperature is 37.8°C. Joint aspirate shows 24,000 WBC/µL (mostly neutrophils), a Gram stain with no organisms, and needle-shaped crystals that are yellow when parallel to the axis of the compensator. Which mechanism best explains his condition?
choices: Increased purine synthesis due to HGPRT deficiency
Reduced renal excretion of uric acid
Deposition of calcium pyrophosphate in cartilage
Overproduction of uric acid from rapid cell turnover
Bacterial seeding of the joint during bacteremia
questions.explanation: Needle-shaped, **negatively birefringent** crystals in the first MTP joint (**podagra**) mean **gout**. Most gout comes from **underexcretion** of uric acid: **thiazides** lower renal urate excretion, and alcohol adds to the problem. Overproduction from rapid cell turnover fits leukemia or tumor lysis, which this man does not have. HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan) presents in childhood with neurologic and behavioral problems.
questions.explanation_pt: Cristais em agulha com **birrefringência negativa** na primeira MTF (**podagra**) indicam **gota**. A maior parte dos casos de gota decorre da **hipoexcreção** de ácido úrico: os **tiazídicos** reduzem a excreção renal de urato, e o álcool agrava o quadro. A hiperprodução por alta renovação celular ocorre em leucemia ou lise tumoral, que este paciente não tem. A deficiência de HGPRT (Lesch-Nyhan) se manifesta na infância com alterações neurológicas e comportamentais.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman has 2 days of sudden pain and swelling in her right knee. She has primary hyperparathyroidism. Temperature is 37.9°C. The knee is warm with a large effusion. An x-ray shows thin linear calcification within the knee cartilage. Synovial fluid has 18,000 WBC/µL (mostly neutrophils), a Gram stain with no organisms, and rhomboid crystals that are weakly positively birefringent. Which substance are these crystals most likely made of?
questions.explanation: Rhomboid, **weakly positively birefringent** crystals plus **chondrocalcinosis** in an older patient with **hyperparathyroidism** mean **pseudogout** (CPPD disease); the crystals are **calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate**. Monosodium urate crystals (gout) are needle-shaped and **negatively** birefringent, and gout most often starts in the first MTP joint. Basic calcium phosphate crystals are too small to see as distinct crystals under polarized light, and they are not birefringent.
questions.explanation_pt: Cristais romboides com **birrefringência fracamente positiva** e **condrocalcinose** em paciente idosa com **hiperparatireoidismo** indicam **pseudogota** (doença por deposição de pirofosfato de cálcio); os cristais são de **pirofosfato de cálcio di-hidratado**. Os cristais de urato monossódico (gota) são em agulha e têm birrefringência **negativa**, e a gota costuma começar na primeira MTF. Os cristais de fosfato básico de cálcio são pequenos demais para serem vistos como cristais individuais à luz polarizada e não são birrefringentes.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman has 4 months of pain and swelling in both hands. Her hands are stiff for more than an hour each morning and improve with activity. Exam shows symmetric swelling of the wrists, the metacarpophalangeal joints and the proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands. The distal interphalangeal joints are normal. Her left knee also has an effusion. Knee aspirate is cloudy yellow fluid with 14,000 WBC/µL (70% neutrophils), no crystals, and a Gram stain with no organisms. Which antibody is most specific for her diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Symmetric polyarthritis of the wrists, MCP and PIP joints with **DIP sparing** and long morning stiffness, plus **inflammatory** synovial fluid without crystals or bacteria, means **rheumatoid arthritis**. **Anti-CCP** antibody is the most specific test. Rheumatoid factor is common in RA but less specific: it also appears in hepatitis C, Sjögren syndrome, other chronic infections and healthy older people.
questions.explanation_pt: Poliartrite simétrica de punhos, MCF e IFP **poupando as IFD**, com rigidez matinal prolongada, e líquido sinovial **inflamatório** sem cristais nem bactérias, indicam **artrite reumatoide**. O **anti-CCP** é o exame mais específico. O fator reumatoide é comum na AR, mas é menos específico: também aparece na hepatite C, na síndrome de Sjögren, em outras infecções crônicas e em idosos saudáveis.

notes.title: Arthritis and crystal disease: patterns, crystals and joint fluid
notes.body_md:
## Degenerative vs autoimmune

- **Osteoarthritis**: cartilage wear, **osteophytes**, subchondral sclerosis; **Heberden** (DIP) and **Bouchard** (PIP) nodes; no systemic inflammation.
- **Rheumatoid arthritis**: **HLA-DR4**, symmetric MCP, PIP and wrist synovitis that **spares the DIP**; morning stiffness over an hour; **pannus** erodes bone. **Anti-CCP** is the most specific antibody.
- **Juvenile idiopathic arthritis**: arthritis that starts before age 16 and lasts at least 6 weeks; the oligoarticular, ANA-positive form carries a risk of silent **anterior uveitis**.

## Seronegative spondyloarthropathies (HLA-B27, RF negative)

- **Ankylosing spondylitis**: sacroiliitis, **bamboo spine**, uveitis, aortic regurgitation.
- **Psoriatic arthritis**: DIP disease, **dactylitis**, nail pitting, **pencil-in-cup**.
- **Reactive arthritis**: arthritis, conjunctivitis and urethritis after *Chlamydia* or enteric infection.
- **IBD-associated arthritis**: with Crohn disease or ulcerative colitis.

## Crystal arthritis

- **Gout**: monosodium urate, **needle-shaped**, **negatively birefringent**; **podagra**, **tophi**; mostly from **underexcretion**.
- **Pseudogout** (CPPD): **rhomboid**, **weakly positively birefringent**; knee; **chondrocalcinosis**.
- Crystals do not rule out infection; a joint can have both.
- Drugs: see the musculoskeletal pharmacology block.

## Infectious arthritis

- **Staphylococcus aureus**: most common cause of septic arthritis.
- **Neisseria gonorrhoeae**: young sexually active adults; migratory arthralgia, tenosynovitis, pustules.
- **Borrelia burgdorferi** (Lyme arthritis): large joints, often the knee.

## Synovial fluid (approximate WBC/µL)

- **Noninflammatory** (OA, trauma): clear and viscous, under about 2,000.
- **Inflammatory** (RA, crystals, spondyloarthropathies): cloudy, about 2,000 to 50,000, often neutrophils.
- **Septic**: purulent, usually above 50,000 with mostly neutrophils; Gram stain and culture.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Degenerativa vs autoimune

- **Osteoartrite**: desgaste da cartilagem, **osteófitos**, esclerose subcondral; nódulos de **Heberden** (IFD) e de **Bouchard** (IFP); sem inflamação sistêmica.
- **Artrite reumatoide**: **HLA-DR4**, sinovite simétrica de MCF, IFP e punhos que **poupa as IFD**; rigidez matinal maior que uma hora; o **pannus** erode o osso. O **anti-CCP** é o anticorpo mais específico.
- **Artrite idiopática juvenil**: artrite que começa antes dos 16 anos e dura pelo menos 6 semanas; a forma oligoarticular com FAN positivo traz risco de **uveíte anterior** silenciosa.

## Espondiloartropatias soronegativas (HLA-B27, FR negativo)

- **Espondilite anquilosante**: sacroileíte, **coluna em bambu**, uveíte, insuficiência aórtica.
- **Artrite psoriásica**: acometimento das IFD, **dactilite**, *pitting* ungueal, **lápis na taça** (*pencil-in-cup*).
- **Artrite reativa**: artrite, conjuntivite e uretrite após infecção por *Chlamydia* ou entérica.
- **Artrite associada à DII**: com doença de Crohn ou retocolite ulcerativa.

## Artrite por cristais

- **Gota**: urato monossódico, **em agulha**, **birrefringência negativa**; **podagra**, **tofos**; principalmente por **hipoexcreção**.
- **Pseudogota** (doença por depósito de pirofosfato de cálcio): cristais **romboides**, **birrefringência fracamente positiva**; joelho; **condrocalcinose**.
- Cristais não excluem infecção; a articulação pode ter as duas coisas.
- Medicamentos: ver o bloco de farmacologia musculoesquelética.

## Artrite infecciosa

- **Staphylococcus aureus**: causa mais comum de artrite séptica.
- **Neisseria gonorrhoeae**: adultos jovens sexualmente ativos; artralgia migratória, tenossinovite, pústulas.
- **Borrelia burgdorferi** (artrite de Lyme): grandes articulações, geralmente o joelho.

## Líquido sinovial (leucócitos/µL aproximados)

- **Não inflamatório** (OA, trauma): límpido e viscoso, abaixo de cerca de 2.000.
- **Inflamatório** (AR, cristais, espondiloartropatias): turvo, cerca de 2.000 a 50.000, frequentemente neutrófilos.
- **Séptico**: purulento, geralmente acima de 50.000 com predomínio de neutrófilos; Gram e cultura.
